source_evidence.anchor: Introduction, definition of QR factorization and Householder reduction
source_evidence.observation: The paper's standing QR setting has A in R^(m x n) with m >= n, an orthogonal Q in R^(m x m), and an upper-trapezoidal R in R^(m x n); a sequence of Householder matrices reduces A to R.

source_evidence.anchor: norm and constant conventions preceding Theorem 1.1
source_evidence.observation: The paper defines the vector 2-norm, the corresponding subordinate matrix norm, and the Frobenius norm ||A||_F = trace(A^T A)^(1/2), denotes the jth column of A by a_j, and declares c_0,c_1,c_2,... to be integer constants of modest size.

The standard arithmetic model is fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u. Equation (1.6) defines gamma_tilde_k(lambda) = exp((lambda*sqrt(k)*u + k*u^2)/(1-u)) - 1 = lambda*sqrt(k)*u + O(u^2), with lambda > 0.
Chronologically ordered errors are mean independent when E(delta_k | delta_(k-1),...,delta_1) = E(delta_k) for k = 2:k_max.
The probabilistic rounding model requires the generated errors, in computation order, to satisfy (1.4) and to be mean-independent random variables of mean zero.

For the perturbed Householder factors, equation (4.2) is ||Delta P_j||_2 <= c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda), simultaneously for all transformation indices j; Lemma 4.1 itself obtains this only with probability at least 1 - 2rm exp(-lambda^2/2).

The remaining section results explicitly assume that (4.2) holds with probability 1 for every j. Lemma 4.2 then gives a first-order vector backward-error bound with coefficient c_6 lambda sqrt(r) gamma_tilde_m(lambda).

Applying the vector result to every column yields ||Delta a_j||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(r) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||a_j||_2 + O(u^2), j = 1:n. The proof uses a union bound to make these column inequalities simultaneous with probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2).

For the computed upper-trapezoidal Householder QR factor R_hat, under Model 1.5 and Lemma 4.2's assumption, there exists an orthogonal Q such that A + Delta A = Q R_hat. Simultaneously for j = 1:n, ||Delta a_j||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||a_j||_2 + O(u^2), with probability at least p_4(lambda,m,n) = 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2).

The proof accounts for explicitly zeroed entries and for computed Householder vectors. It says the vector-construction error contributes a perturbation of order u c_4 gamma_tilde_m(lambda) = O(u^2), so it does not alter the first-order coefficient in (4.17).

The paper characterizes the first-order dependence as sqrt(mn)u and the second-order dependence as mn^2u^2. It states m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 as the effective requirement for the first-order growth interpretation, while noting that this is not a stated premise of equation (4.20).

source_evidence.anchor: implication sentence preceding equation (4.20) and equation (4.20)
source_evidence.observation: The paper states that the columnwise bound (4.17) implies ||Delta A||_F <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||A||_F + O(u^2). The coefficient is unchanged by the columnwise-to-Frobenius passage.

binders: m and n are matrix dimensions, A is in R^(m x n), and Delta A has the same dimensions; the standing Householder-QR setting has m >= n. [PDF p. 1, Introduction QR definition; PDF p. 10, text following (4.19)]
For each j = 1:n, a_j and Delta a_j denote the jth columns of A and Delta A. [PDF p. 2, column convention; PDF p. 9, equation (4.17)]
u is the unit roundoff used in the standard relative-error model. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.4)]
lambda is a real probability parameter with lambda > 0. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6)]
c_6 is one of the paper's fixed integer constants of modest size. [PDF p. 2, constant convention; PDF p. 9, equation (4.17)]

In the enclosing theorem, R_hat in R^(m x n) is the computed upper-trapezoidal Householder QR factor, while Q in R^(m x m) and Delta A are existential outputs. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.16)]
hypotheses: The direct premise of the selected implication is the simultaneous family ||Delta a_j||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||a_j||_2 + O(u^2) for every j = 1:n. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17) and Lemma 4.3 proof]
For the probabilistic Householder-QR provenance of that premise, R_hat must be obtained from A by the Householder QR algorithm. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4]
The rounding errors satisfy Model 1.5: chronological mean independence, mean zero, and the standard relative-error bound. [PDF p. 3, Model 1.5; PDF p. 2, equation (1.4)]

The theorem additionally assumes Lemma 4.2's idealized premise that ||Delta P_j||_2 <= c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda) holds with probability 1 for every applied Householder transformation. [PDF p. 6, equation (4.2); PDF p. 7, sentence preceding Lemma 4.2]

The condition m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 is not a formal premise of the displayed implication; it is introduced afterward for interpreting the retained first-order term as dominant. [PDF p. 10, equation (4.18) and surrounding discussion]
conclusions: The selected normwise conclusion is ||Delta A||_F <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||A||_F + O(u^2). [PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]

The columnwise-to-Frobenius implication retains exactly the coefficient c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda); it introduces no additional factor of sqrt(n). [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
In the enclosing Householder-QR theorem, the perturbation is a backward error satisfying A + Delta A = Q R_hat for an exact orthogonal Q. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.16)]

Because (4.17) is simultaneous with probability at least p_4(lambda,m,n), (4.20) holds on that same event and hence inherits that probability lower bound; equation (4.20) does not restate it. [PDF p. 9, Lemma 4.3 proof and Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 10, implication sentence before (4.20)]
definitions_and_conventions: gamma_tilde_k(lambda) means exp((lambda*sqrt(k)*u + k*u^2)/(1-u)) - 1, with expansion lambda*sqrt(k)*u + O(u^2). In (4.17) and (4.20), k = m. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6); PDF pp. 9-10, equations (4.17) and (4.20)]
The vector norm is ||x||_2 = (x^T x)^(1/2), and the Frobenius norm is ||A||_F = trace(A^T A)^(1/2). [PDF p. 2, norm convention]
The notation a_j denotes column j of A; correspondingly, Delta a_j denotes column j of Delta A in (4.17). [PDF p. 2, column convention; PDF p. 9, equation (4.17)]
The constants c_i are integer constants of modest size rather than task-specific variables with values supplied by the theorem. [PDF p. 2, constant convention]
Mean independence is chronological conditional-mean independence, not mutual stochastic independence. [PDF p. 2, Definition 1.3; PDF p. 3, Model 1.5]
implicit_context: The restriction m >= n is inherited from the paper's definition of the Householder QR problem and is reiterated in the post-theorem discussion, although Theorem 4.4 does not repeat it in its opening sentence. [PDF p. 1, Introduction QR definition; PDF p. 10, text following (4.19)]

The restriction lambda > 0 is inherited from the definition of gamma_tilde rather than repeated in Theorem 4.4 or equation (4.20). [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6); PDF pp. 9-10, equations (4.17) and (4.20)]
The randomness is over the rounding errors generated by the computation; A and the algorithmic dimensions are treated as fixed inputs. [PDF p. 3, Model 1.5; PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4]

The selected implication is algebraic once all column bounds hold; the algorithmic and probabilistic assumptions explain why that simultaneous premise is available. [PDF p. 9, Lemma 4.3 proof and equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, implication sentence before (4.20)]
The same-event probability for (4.20) is inherited by implication and is not separately printed next to (4.20). [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is linked specifically to the standard Householder QR algorithm producing the computed upper-trapezoidal factor R_hat. The theorem supplies an exact orthogonal Q and a backward perturbation Delta A with A + Delta A = Q R_hat. The Frobenius implication itself only uses the simultaneous column bounds and does not otherwise depend on Householder structure. [PDF p. 1, Householder QR description; PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4 and equations (4.16)-(4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
numerical_model: Each elementary operation is modeled by fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), with |delta| <= u. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.4)]
The generated rounding errors, ordered chronologically, are mean independent and have mean zero. [PDF p. 3, Model 1.5; PDF p. 2, Definition 1.3]

The theorem also uses the stronger probability-one assumption for every local Householder perturbation bound (4.2), even though Lemma 4.1 derives that bound only with probability at least 1 - 2rm exp(-lambda^2/2). [PDF p. 6, Lemma 4.1 and equation (4.2); PDF p. 7, sentence preceding Lemma 4.2]
The simultaneous column event has lower-bound probability p_4(lambda,m,n) = 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2). [PDF p. 9, Lemma 4.3 proof and Theorem 4.4]
error_notions: Delta A is a normwise and columnwise backward perturbation of the input A, certified by the exact relation A + Delta A = Q R_hat. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.16)]
Equation (4.17) measures each perturbation column in the vector 2-norm relative to the corresponding input-column 2-norm, plus an additive higher-order term. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17)]
Equation (4.20) measures the whole perturbation and input in the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
Q is exact and orthogonal, while R_hat is computed; the selected result is not a forward-error or computed-Q orthogonality statement. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.16)]
norms: The column inequalities use the Euclidean vector 2-norm. [PDF p. 2, norm convention; PDF p. 9, equation (4.17)]
The local Householder perturbation premise uses the corresponding subordinate matrix 2-norm. [PDF p. 2, norm convention; PDF p. 6, equation (4.2)]
The matrix conclusion uses the Frobenius norm defined by trace(A^T A)^(1/2). [PDF p. 2, norm convention; PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]

The implication relies on the column decomposition ||A||_F^2 = sum_(j=1)^n ||a_j||_2^2 and its analogue for Delta A; this identity follows from the stated Frobenius definition but is not separately displayed beside (4.20). [PDF p. 2, Frobenius definition; PDF p. 10, implication sentence before (4.20)]
constants_and_indexing: The column index is exactly j = 1:n, and the probability statement applies to all these columns simultaneously. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17) and Lemma 4.3 proof]
The exact first-order multiplier in both the premise and conclusion is C = c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda). [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
No additional sqrt(n), n, or column-count factor appears when passing to the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]

For Householder QR, the sequence length r in Lemmas 4.2-4.3 is specialized to n, producing sqrt(n) in Theorem 4.4. [PDF p. 9, equations (4.15)-(4.17) and proof; PDF p. 9, post-theorem instruction to set r = n]
The probability lower bound is exactly 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2), with no factor 1/2 in the exponent. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4]

Using equation (1.6) with fixed lambda, the displayed multiplier has leading form c_6 lambda^2 sqrt(mn)u; the paper summarizes only the dimension dependence as sqrt(mn)u while treating lambda as a modest constant. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6); PDF p. 10, conclusion following (4.20)]
higher_order_terms: Both the column premise (4.17) and Frobenius conclusion (4.20) retain an additive O(u^2) term. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
Theorem 4.4 is explicitly described as a first-order backward-error result, unlike the all-orders worst-case Theorem 1.1. [PDF p. 9, paragraph following the proof of Theorem 4.4]
The computed Householder-vector error is absorbed into O(u^2) and does not change the displayed first-order coefficient. [PDF p. 9, proof of Theorem 4.4 following equation (4.17)]
The omitted second-order contribution is described as having mn^2u^2 dependence, compared with sqrt(mn)u at first order. [PDF p. 10, discussion preceding equation (4.18)]

The condition m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 is required only for the claim that the first-order term governs the growth; it is not printed as a hypothesis of the columnwise-to-Frobenius implication. [PDF p. 10, equation (4.18) and equation (4.20)]
exceptional_values: The cited theorem states no full-rank, nonsingularity, or nonzero-column hypothesis on A. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4]
The inspected arithmetic-model passage does not specify behavior for overflow, underflow, subnormals, NaNs, or infinities; it only states the relative-error model (1.4). [PDF p. 2, equation (1.4)]

Equation (1.6) contains the denominator 1-u, but the cited passage gives no explicit admissible range for u beyond identifying it as unit roundoff and using the standard model. [PDF p. 2, equations (1.4) and (1.6)]

Only lambda > 0 is stated; no additional restriction is imposed to make 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2) positive, so for small lambda the displayed probability lower bound may be vacuous. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6); PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4]

undebatable_constraints: The selected result is an implication from bounds for every column j = 1:n to a Frobenius-norm bound. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, sentence before equation (4.20)]
The column premise must be simultaneous across all n columns, not a separate per-column event with an unspecified joint probability. [PDF p. 9, Lemma 4.3 proof and Theorem 4.4]
The premise and conclusion use the identical coefficient c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda). [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
No additional sqrt(n) factor may be introduced in the Frobenius conclusion. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
gamma_tilde_m(lambda) must use the exact definition exp((lambda*sqrt(m)*u + m*u^2)/(1-u)) - 1, and lambda must satisfy lambda > 0. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6)]

The O(u^2) remainder printed in every column bound and in the Frobenius conclusion must not be silently deleted or changed into an exact zero remainder. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)]
The matrix conclusion is in the Frobenius norm, while each column premise is in the vector 2-norm. [PDF p. 2, norm convention; PDF pp. 9-10, equations (4.17) and (4.20)]

In the enclosing theorem, Delta A is a backward perturbation satisfying A + Delta A = Q R_hat with Q exact and orthogonal and R_hat computed by Householder QR. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.16)]

The probabilistic provenance requires Model 1.5 and the probability-one form of Lemma 4.2's local perturbation premise. [PDF p. 3, Model 1.5; PDF pp. 6-7, equation (4.2) and Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4]

The simultaneous column bounds hold with probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2), and the deterministic implication places (4.20) on that same event. [PDF p. 9, Lemma 4.3 proof and Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 10, implication before (4.20)]

The first-order scaling interpretation must not be presented as an all-orders bound; the paper explicitly retains O(u^2) and discusses a separate dominance condition. [PDF pp. 9-10, discussion following Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.18)]

ambiguities.issue: The hidden content and uniformity of the additive O(u^2) terms are unspecified.
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.17) and (4.20) print bare additive O(u^2) terms without naming constants, dependence on m, n, lambda, or column norms, or a common remainder valid uniformly in j. The following discussion only estimates aggregate orders. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, text preceding (4.18) and equation (4.20)]
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must either retain an abstract remainder with explicit uniform bounds or deliberately restrict itself to the displayed first-order coefficient; it cannot infer an exact remainder-free inequality from the paper.

ambiguities.issue: Equation (4.20) does not restate a probability.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.4 attaches p_4(lambda,m,n) to the simultaneous family (4.17), while the later prose merely says that (4.17) implies (4.20). [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 10, sentence before equation (4.20)]
ambiguities.impact: The same probability for (4.20) is a logical inheritance from the simultaneous event, not an independently stated probabilistic claim.

ambiguities.issue: The selected implication can be read either as a standalone deterministic norm lemma or as a corollary within the probabilistic Householder-QR theorem.
ambiguities.evidence: The implication sentence itself references only the columnwise bound (4.17), whereas (4.17) comes from Theorem 4.4 under algorithmic, rounding-model, and probability-one assumptions. [PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, implication before (4.20)]
ambiguities.impact: A standalone formalization needs only the simultaneous column premise; a faithful formalization of the paper theorem must additionally preserve its Householder-QR and probabilistic provenance.

ambiguities.issue: The exact numerical values of c_5 and c_6 are not supplied.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper globally describes all c_i as integer constants of modest size and uses c_5 and c_6 symbolically in (4.2), (4.17), and (4.20). [PDF p. 2, constant convention; PDF p. 6, equation (4.2); PDF pp. 9-10, equations (4.17) and (4.20)]
ambiguities.impact: The contract fixes the symbolic coefficient but cannot instantiate it as a particular numeral.

ambiguities.issue: The asymptotic regime behind O(u^2) is not explicitly quantified.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (1.6) and the later error bounds use O(u^2), while the higher-order discussion varies dimensions and compares dimension-dependent terms without defining which parameters are held fixed in the big-O notation. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6); PDF pp. 9-10, equations (4.17)-(4.20)]
ambiguities.impact: A formal asymptotic interpretation must state whether m, n, and lambda are fixed and how hidden constants depend on them.

ambiguities.issue: The probability-one local perturbation premise is an explicit idealization rather than a consequence of Model 1.5 alone.
ambiguities.evidence: Lemma 4.1 obtains (4.2) with probability at least 1 - 2rm exp(-lambda^2/2), but the paper then assumes probability 1 for all j and later acknowledges replacing the high probability by 1. [PDF p. 6, Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 7, sentence preceding Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 10, paragraph preceding equation (4.20)]
ambiguities.impact: The assumption must remain explicit in any theorem-level contract and must not be presented as derived solely from mean-independent, zero-mean rounding errors.

ambiguities.issue: The valid range of u and exceptional IEEE behavior are not specified in the selected context.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper states (1.4) and defines gamma_tilde using 1-u in the denominator, but the inspected passage gives no explicit overflow, underflow, subnormal, NaN, infinity, or precise u-range assumptions. [PDF p. 2, equations (1.4) and (1.6)]
ambiguities.impact: A machine-level formalization needs additional assumptions before claiming coverage of exceptional floating-point cases.

contract_plain_english: For an m-by-n matrix A and a perturbation Delta A, assume that every column j = 1:n simultaneously satisfies ||Delta a_j||_2 <= C||a_j||_2 + O(u^2), where C is exactly c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda). Then ||Delta A||_F <= C||A||_F + O(u^2), with no additional column-count factor. [PDF p. 9, equation (4.17); PDF p. 10, equation (4.20)] Here gamma_tilde_m(lambda) = exp((lambda*sqrt(m)*u + m*u^2)/(1-u)) - 1 and lambda > 0. [PDF p. 2, equation (1.6)] In the enclosing result, R_hat is the computed upper-trapezoidal Householder QR factor, there is an exact orthogonal Q with A + Delta A = Q R_hat, and the simultaneous column event has probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2) under Model 1.5 and the probability-one assumption from Lemma 4.2. [PDF p. 3, Model 1.5; PDF pp. 6-7, equation (4.2) and Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 9, Theorem 4.4] The additive O(u^2) terms and their hidden dependence are not specified precisely and must therefore be preserved as an ambiguity rather than discarded. [PDF pp. 9-10, equations (4.17)-(4.20)]
